record.tranche_reason: The study causally investigates a related induction-style mechanism and its development, but uses a different task and measurements from the original work. It reports a sequence of circuit components emerging across checkpoints, rather than measuring the original training-loss bump and token-index loss measure.
record.gate_note: The paper reports no training-loss curve or loss falling with token index, so it does not test the claimed loss bump or that specific in-context-learning measure. Results attributed to cited prior work are not recorded. The paper’s own checkpoint results measure repeated-label copying, withholding on unique-label prompts, and class-keyed retrieval.
record.test_reason: The study's main object is a gated class-keyed retrieval circuit for few-shot sentence classification in 3–4B models. This is related to induction heads, not the same construct. Its one direct result on classic induction heads is in Section 9 and Figure 17: in Llama-3.2-3B, heads picked by a generic induction score hold the readers on the sink, and ablating them raises the margin by about a nat. That bears on whether few-shot task learning runs through induction heads (V6) in a new setting. The loss bump, token-index loss and canonical [A][B]…[A]→[B] completion are never measured.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. Add that the authors describe the readers as induction heads keyed on a class, and the duplicate-token detectors as the first half of the induction circuit repurposed to signal a repeat. In the scratch model, slots and readers form under all distributions, and only the gate needs penalised unique-label retrieval.
record.recipe_differences: Causal activation patching, head ablations, steering, and checkpoint measurements on sentence-class retrieval; not a direct reproduction of the original induction-head training/loss procedure.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary with model family and size, training checkpoint, and scratch-training distribution. Gate steering in the scratch-trained model is partial and seed-dependent.

fits_no_version.finding: Few-shot classification is carried by upper-layer 'reader' heads that match the query's class against class keys at label tokens and copy the label. The authors call these 'induction heads keyed on a class'. Reader handoffs carry about 60% (Qwen), about 100% (SmolLM3) and 45–54% (Llama) of a class flip.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Class-keyed (abstract) induction-like heads carry few-shot label retrieval in pretrained LMs.

fits_no_version.finding: Duplicate-token heads (first half of the induction circuit) feed a gate direction that opens retrieval. A model trained from scratch grows the gate only when unique-label retrieval is penalised.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Repeat detection from duplicate-token heads gates in-context retrieval, and its formation depends on training data.

fits_no_version.finding: In OLMo-2, label copying is present first, withholding appears next, and class-keyed retrieval last (7B only). A scratch model learns the task abruptly between 8k and 30k steps.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The ICL classification circuit assembles in a fixed order across training.

record.problems: The studied task is narrow sentence classification, not general ICL. OLMo checkpoint measurements use 30 prompts per point and the checkpoints are sparse; the paper reports no training-loss curve or bump. Some checkpoint and scratch-model results have no reported uncertainty intervals. The scratch-trained model is small and synthetic.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted due to the 60-row limit. Other circuit measurements were not included where they did not directly bear on the listed claim versions.

untested.parts: No small attention-only model is trained, and previous-token composition is not tested. The hand-built attention-only model is hand-set, so it says nothing about formation.
No loss curve, loss bump or token-index ICL measure. OLMo checkpoints are too sparse and start after copying is already present.
No loss-versus-token-index measure and no broad ICL coverage.
Token-level induction heads are not counted across models. Class-keyed readers are a related but different construct.
Data dependence is shown for the gate only. Slots and readers form under all three training distributions. Induction-head formation and ICL persistence are not measured.
The staged order (copying, then withholding, then class retrieval) concerns the broader circuit. It does not concern sub-steps of induction-head formation.

missing.what: Llama-3.2-3B: knocking out the 16 heads with the highest generic induction scores moves middle-layer readers off the sink and raises the margin by about a nat.
Qwen3-4B: knocking out the 16 induction-scored heads leaves the gate at +14.0 / −7.4, against −0.3 / −19.1 for the duplicate-token heads.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's links treated class-keyed readers, the gate and circuit-assembly stages as induction heads. The study's own construct is a generalised, class-keyed lookup in 3–4B models with MLPs, so most rows are re-linked to none. The only direct result on induction-scored heads (Llama, Qwen) is missing from the rows. Preprint.

versions.untested_parts: Does not directly test canonical [A][B] … [A] → [B] completion or show that the class-keyed readers compose with a previous-token head in the original induction-head construction. The attention-only model is hand-built; the pretrained models are not attention-only.
No training-loss bump or token-index loss measure; checkpoint observations do not establish the width of a transition window or synchrony with a loss-curve feature.
The study examines narrow sentence-class retrieval, not most in-context learning across large transformers, and does not measure loss falling with token index.
Tests related circuit components across several transformer models, sizes and checkpoints; does not establish canonical induction behaviour in other architectures or modalities.

Tests how training-data conditions affect the gate in a small synthetic task and reports checkpoint order in OLMo-2. It does not comprehensively test data and training dependencies across pretrained model families or whether ICL generally persists.
Tests the causal role of class-keyed readers and other circuit parts in sentence classification, but does not compare few-shot task learning across a broad set of tasks or systems.
The checkpoint study distinguishes copying, withholding and class-keyed retrieval, but does not resolve the detailed timing of every subcomponent or establish transitions from a training-loss curve.

rows.subject: Qwen3-4B-Base
rows.operation_detail: Mean-ablated sixteen duplicate-token heads and measured the gate projection on recurring-label prompts.
rows.measure: Projection on gate direction g
rows.value: with duplicate-token heads ablated: −0.3
rows.note: Sixteen random heads moved the projection by at most 0.7; the sixteen highest induction-score heads moved it by 4.2. The duplicate-token heads attend to earlier copies of the same label token and affect the repeat signal, not the class-keyed lookup directly.
rows.check: Measures projection on the gate direction, a feature, not induction behaviour. Duplicate-token heads are only the first half of the induction circuit. The induction-scored comparison (moved 4.2) belongs in a V6 row instead.

rows.subject: OLMo-2 1B
rows.operation_detail: Measured repeated-label copying at the earliest reported checkpoint and tested the effect of ablating duplicate-token heads.
rows.measure: Correct-label margin and effect of duplicate-token-head knockout
rows.value: with sixteen duplicate-token heads knocked out: −1.96; repeated-label copying is reported present from the first checkpoint
rows.note: The paper reports that recurring prompts have the label as argmax at every OLMo checkpoint.
rows.check: Repeated-label copying is already present at the first checkpoint (21B tokens), so neither abruptness nor a narrow window nor coincidence with a loss bump can be read. It is not a V7 measure.

rows.subject: Four-layer, eight-head Llama-architecture model (3.4M parameters)
rows.operation_detail: Trained on the synthetic task and measured when the task was learned.

conditions.value: mix and recurring-only distributions; three seeds each
synthetic sentence classification with arbitrary labels

rows.measure: Task-learning margin over training
rows.value: Task learned abruptly between 8k and 30k steps; by 40k steps every run answered both prompt kinds with a margin near 10 nats
rows.note: The paper does not report a training-loss bump or measure whether the task transition coincides with one.
rows.check: Abrupt learning of a synthetic class-retrieval task. Induction-head formation and the loss curve are not tracked, and the 8k–30k window is wide relative to the 40k-step run.

rows.subject: Four-layer, eight-head Llama-architecture model (3.4M parameters)
rows.operation_detail: Trained on a mix of unique-label and recurring-label prompts, with consistent unique-label mappings.

rows.value: Gate absent in the reported runs: gate-direction held-out sign accuracy across the six runs was 0.45–0.62, and steering was not consistent; the mix condition’s displayed seed had margins 8.8 nats on both unique and recurring prompts
rows.note: The paper says unique-label retrieval is not penalized under this training distribution.
rows.check: Gate formation is not induction-head formation. Slots and readers form under every distribution.

rows.subject: Four-layer, eight-head Llama-architecture model (3.4M parameters)

rows.subject: Four-layer, eight-head Llama-architecture model (3.4M parameters)

conditions.value: recurring-to-unique or unique-to-recurring; outcomes varied by seed

rows.subject: Qwen3-4B-Base
rows.operation_detail: Patched the changed prompt’s keys at label-token positions in layers 21–29 for a class-flipped demonstration sentence.

conditions.value: one demonstration sentence changed to the other class; label unchanged

rows.measure: Change in answer margin carried by the key handoff
rows.value: label-token keys in layers 21–29 carried −2.35 nats
rows.note: The result supports class information being written into label-token keys and later read; the same-class sentence control changed the answer by +0.08 nats.
rows.check: Class key at label-token keys in a 4B model with MLPs. Not the V1 mechanism (small attention-only models, previous-token composition).

relationships.reason: Based on text, since no row records it: ablating the 16 heads picked by a generic induction score raises the margin ~1 nat, as these heads hold readers on the sink (Sec. 9, Fig. 17c). In Qwen, induction-scored heads only modestly move the gate (Table 6).
relationships.display_finding: Ablating 16 heads selected by a generic induction score increased the Llama-3.2-3B classification margin by about 1 nat, while induction-scored heads changed the gate only modestly in Qwen.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.reason: Section 9 reports that ablating sixteen generically induction-scored heads raises the margin by about one nat; Figure 17c shows readers released from the sink. Support concerns this head-identification method and task.

labels.label: supports
labels.reason: Section 9 reports that ablating sixteen generically induction-scored heads raises the margin by about one nat; Figure 17c shows readers released from the sink. Support concerns this head-identification method and task.

tranche.reason: Causal interventions on induction-scored heads provide a result in a new sentence-class retrieval setting; this is not a reproduction of the original training and loss measurements.

source_check.notes: The authors also describe the class-keyed readers as induction heads, so the V6 result depends on head definition. V2.method_sensitivity[0] cites r2 but makes no explicit assertion about this study.

statements.correction: Section 5: recurring-label gate projection changes by a reported 4.2 under induction-head ablation. Table 6: recurring projection +18.3 intact versus +14.0 ablated; unique projection −20.9 intact versus −7.4 ablated.
statements.problem: The Llama result is correct. The unqualified description of Qwen's gate movement as modest omits the larger change on unique-label prompts.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Causal sentence-class retrieval and repeated-label detection in the tested models
reader_labels.reason: Key handoffs carry the sentence-class change, query heads carry part of the query flip, and reader interventions affect retrieval (r1, r12–r17). The study’s mechanism is related to, but not a direct test of, canonical token induction.

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.reason: The reported sequence separates repeated-label copying, withholding, and class-keyed retrieval; the 1B model never develops retrieval, while 7B retrieval appears later (r2–r6). No training-loss bump was measured.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Tested Qwen3 sizes, SmolLM3-3B, Llama-3.2-3B, OLMo-2 7B checkpoints, and Qwen3-4B instruct
reader_labels.reason: Related reader and retrieval effects are reported across families, sizes, checkpoints, and an instruct model, though head identities and implementation vary (r16–r23).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Synthetic scratch-trained model: mix, recurring-only, and gate training distributions
reader_labels.reason: The gate is absent in the two control distributions and appears when retrieval on unique-label prompts is penalized; steering it changes margins in a seed-dependent way (r8–r11).

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.reason: The reader set causally carries a substantial share of the class-flip effect and its knockout reduces the margin, rather than task retrieval running mainly through unrelated heads (r14–r15). The study also finds important complementary circuit parts (r24).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: The reported components appear in sequence: repeated-label copying first, then withholding, then class-keyed retrieval in 7B; the 1B model lacks the final retrieval stage (r2–r6).
